info.title: Stars Auth Direct Auth API
info.description: The authorization challenge endpoint of OAuth 2.0 for First-Party Applications (draft-ietf-oauth-first-party-apps-04). An App signs a User in without a browser and redeems the authorization_code at the OIDC token endpoint (grant_type=authorization_code, with code_verifier and no redirect_uri); the tokens are the ones the OIDC flow issues.

post.description: Code login takes two requests: `identifier` (+ `altcha`) sends a code and answers `insufficient_authorization` with an `auth_session`; `auth_session` + `code` then yields the authorization code. Password login is one request: `username` + `password` (+ `altcha`). Sign in with Apple in an App is one request too: `provider` + `authorization_code`, the code exactly as Sign in with Apple gave it (no identity token, no nonce); a User new to the instance is signed up. Passkey login is two requests: `passkey=begin` with the first request's parameters answers 200 with assertion `options` and an `auth_session`, no `altcha`; the AuthenticationResponseJSON the system credential API returned is then sent as `passkey` on that `auth_session`. After any of these, 两步验证 and phone binding go on by `next` as usual — a Passkey has passed 两步验证 itself, so it never asks for a TOTP. If the instance requires a phone number the User has not bound, signing in answers `insufficient_authorization` instead, and the App sends a code to a phone number and enters it on the same `auth_session`. Confidential Applications authenticate as at the token endpoint (client_secret_basic or client_secret_post).

client_id.description: Required unless auth_session is sent or the client authenticates with HTTP Basic.

scope.description: Space-separated: openid, offline_access, phone, email. Ignored once auth_session is sent.

code_challenge.description: PKCE; required for public Applications. Ignored once auth_session is sent.

auth_session.description: From an earlier insufficient_authorization answer; continues that sign-in.

terms_version.description: The version of the terms the User agreed to (see GET /v1/auth/terms). Once the instance has terms, every request must carry the current version, and signing in records the User's consent to it; until then it may be empty or left out.

altcha.description: ALTCHA PoW solution (challenge from GET /altcha/challenge), base64. Required with identifier and with username.

identifier.description: +86 phone number or email to send a code to.

code.description: The code sent to the identifier of this auth_session.

password.description: The User's password. When it is the initial password of a 待激活 account — an admin created it and the User has not set their own — the answer is 403 `insufficient_authorization` with `next: "password"`: send the new password here on that `auth_session`, with no `altcha`, and the account is activated and the sign-in goes on. This is the one step such a User may take on their own.

provider.description: The Provider ID of an enabled Provider of a type Apps can sign in with (today Apple only), with authorization_code.

authorization_code.description: With provider: what the Provider's SDK gave the App. For Apple, the authorization_code of Sign in with Apple, exchanged once by Stars Auth as the Provider's Bundle ID.

passkey.description: Passkey sign-in (ADR 0014), either of two values. `begin`, with the first request's parameters and no `auth_session`: answers 200 with `options` and an `auth_session`, and requires no `altcha`. Or the AuthenticationResponseJSON the system credential API returned for those options, with that `auth_session`: answers 200 with the authorization code. An assertion that does not verify answers 400 `invalid_request` and spends the `auth_session`; start over. Android Apps are accepted from the `android:apk-key-hash:` origin their registered signing certificate names.

totp.description: A 6-digit code from the User's authenticator, when `next` is `totp`. Each code works once.

delete.description: While an account is 待激活: any non-empty value deletes the account — the 注销 a User is otherwise offered from the account center. Answers 400 `access_denied`.

recovery_code.description: Instead of totp: one of the User's 恢复码 (xxxx-xxxx; any case, dash optional). Each works once.

200.description: Signed in, with `authorization_code`. With `passkey=begin` instead: `auth_session` and `options`, nothing signed in yet.

authorization_code.description: Every step but passkey=begin answers this.

auth_session.description: With passkey=begin: the sign-in it started, to send the assertion with.

options.description: With passkey=begin: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON under publicKey, as the system credential API takes it.

400.description: `invalid_request`: a parameter is missing or wrong, or the User made a mistake (wrong code or password, PoW unsolved, send limit hit, an IP that started too many Passkey sign-ins; `error_description` says which, in words fit to show, and `auth_session` comes back if one was sent — and if one is still usable). A Passkey assertion that does not verify is an `invalid_request` that spends its `auth_session`. `invalid_grant`: the Provider turned authorization_code down (spent, expired, or not for this App); have the User sign in with it again. `access_denied`: the User was disabled during the sign-in. `unauthorized_client`, `invalid_scope`: as at the token endpoint. `invalid_session`: the auth_session is unknown, expired, or spent (each one yields a single authorization code), or the 5th wrong totp or recovery_code ended it; start over. `redirect_to_web` is never sent: every sign-in step the hosted page has, this endpoint has too.

403.description: `insufficient_authorization`: another step is needed, named by `next`; send it with the `auth_session` returned. `next` is `password` when an admin created the account and the User has not replaced the initial password yet; that step comes first, before 两步验证 and the rest.

get.description: What the App's "我已阅读并同意" checkbox links to, and the version to send as terms_version once it is ticked. Stars Auth does not host the texts.

200.description: An empty version means the instance has no terms yet: any terms_version will do, the empty one too.

post.description: Deletes the User and all their data at once, with no grace period: every Session and refresh token ends, the sub is never reused, and their phone number and email are free at once. Applications with a webhook receive user.deleted. The App sends its access token, which must come from a sign-in in the last 10 minutes: show the User a confirmation, sign them in again through the challenge endpoint, then call this with the new access token.

401.description: WWW-Authenticate says why: error="invalid_token" for a missing, expired or invalid token, or one whose Session ended; error="insufficient_user_authentication" with max_age="600" (RFC 9470) when the sign-in is older than 10 minutes.

409.description: The User is the instance's last owner.

next.description: Sent with `insufficient_authorization` only (non-standard, ADR 0010): the step to take. `code`: enter the code just sent. `phone`: bind a phone number (send a code to one, then enter it). `totp`: the User has 两步验证 on; send `totp` or `recovery_code` (comes before `phone`). Values are only ever added, never renamed or removed; treat one you do not know as a failure (ask the User to update the App).
